title: My journey in mallworld
content: I guess let me add my novella here. Will try to keep it as short as I can. The TL;DR: I've gone to mall world every night for 5 years and have explored this world to a large degree. I have kept notes of my dreams most of my life (45 now, started around 12). _*John Noelle*_ To hit the high points of how this mall thing started for me: in a dream like 7 years ago I met a guy named John Noelle. Stuck out to me because I've never had a named dream character before. In the first dream we were just chatting, about what I don't recall. Some number of weeks later he showed up again, this time he took me to a bowling alley and was trying to show me how you can throw a ball in such a way that it will jump lanes. Over the course of 2 weeks that dream continued, and this was the first time in my life I'd had the same dream but with progression across nights. To illustrate, in case it helps you understand why I view this as different: I had a recurring dream for years in my teens that I was at a party and a mastiff attacked me and killed me. Same dream every single time, same way, always. All my dreams were that way: I had a could handle of dream types that just repeated. In the course of my time with John he explained that the lesson was an analog to time and that I was the ball. He was trying to explain to me that it's possible to jump into different lanes, different timeline, but that humans think about timelines wrong, that it's not this multiverse thing and that it was more like a big ocean where there were a lot of currents and you could ride whichever you could get to. I have no idea if or how his lesson relates, and while I heard and retained every word it's been useless to me. Short of like how we all know the design of the time machine from Back To The Future, but that doesn't help us build one or make a flux capacitor more real. _*The light and the dragon*_ After the dreams of John I started having a vision in my waking life of this huge white house on a high mountain and a vast continent at the foot of that mountain that had a large city city. In the other side of the city, opposite that house, was a dragon. This doesn't seem too radical for me: I've studied religions most of my life and this just aligns to most worldviews: good sits opposite evil and we live in between. Boring. Educational, but nothing revelatory. _*Entering the city*_ A little over 5 years ago, so 2 years into having this vision, I had a dream that I went into the city. I was on top of a vast skyscraper with like 10 other people. We were trying to paragliding over to another building. We knew why, but it was never aid why in the dream, so my note just says 'in the dream I knew why, but I don't actually know why.'... Helpful. A couple days later dreamed of the same team, though we'd lost 2 people who fell during the paragliding. We were in the building and climbing down. It was a weird mix of office spaces (cubicles, offices, etc) and department stores. We got to the ground floor and opened the door to go underground and I woke up. A week later we were in the boiler room which was in a vast set of steam tunnels under the structure. A couple days later we came to a door that entered the mall. A few days later I was separated from my team and I find the mall's front door and left. Here I saw that from the outside it wasn't huge: a couple floors, a lot of stores, but it didn't look huge. Oddly it had a hotel and combination office and apartment building attached, and there was a bus station nearby, a boat dock a bit beyond that, and a big festival of tents set up in the parking lot. The skyscrapers I'd seen before were nowhere to be found and the realization that Is entered a skyscraper in a sense city and exited a nondescript mall in a smallish town was strange. _*Expeditioning*_ Over the course of 2 months I explored in and out of that mall: infinitely bigger on the inside. Vast food court. Escalators that were crazy - some floors only had down escalators, no up one to get you there, others that were so fast you'd surely die trying to step on them - and every for a different style, like this was actually a billion floors from a billion different malls crammed together. A vast entry area with a huge pool and a gorgeous fountain with huge glass escalators up and down to other floors that had slides running beside them. I saw the sit-down restaurants, the hospital, the office building, the hotel with the impossibly janky elevator. The steam tunnels below that seemed to go on forever. Into the third month of having these exploratory dreams every 2-5 nights they became nightly. That has not stopped since. For 5 solid years every single night I am in this world. _*Getting a life*_ A lot of folks seem to feel they are trapped in certain places or feel scared or sense malevolence. I've not had that. I do see the stores where staff have evil grins, or the white restaurant where the staff are all in white and seem incredibly sullen, or the seemingly endless hotel hallways that feel like those Backrooms videos, but I've never had a sense of fear, being trapped, or creepyness. Across the years I have built a life here. I have a job, we bought a house, we have an apartment in the office / apartment building. We bought a used, dilapidated bus from the bus hub and made it into an RV. We've taken buses and boats to explore the world on vacation. I've lived through world events there. Some major technology enhancements like personal teleporters for the rich and a fitbit kind of thing that when turned on becomes a glove that lets you "unzip" a 4th spatial dimension where you can store things. A weird water tech that the hotel uses to make walls of water (testing this tech resulted in the entire first floor of the mall flooding out and being inaccessible for 2 days, stranding folks on higher floors). Also events like a storm that took out an entire island a couple years ago and killed tens of thousands. Updates on an ongoing war between the army of the white house on the hill and the dragon's forces. New floors and store openings in the mall. Kidnappings and cringes outside the mall in both the big city and the small town. My job is a bit wildcard there: programmer, shift lead, executive... I've negotiated deals to open restaurants in the mall, written a monitoring application for the steam tunnels, and led teams into the tunnels to fix burst pipes and such. It's a stressful job, and the people I work with are largely frustrating to deal with. My bosses are seemingly the folks who run the world, and I've met the guy who claims to be responsible for preventing lucid dreaming here. I've found the mall, while huge, has only 3 entrances: the main external one that you get to from the parking lot in town, the steam tunnels one accessible from many other parts of the world, and the roof accessible from the city. Aside from some oddities the world seems a pretty normal world. That makes it more frustrating to me because I have a long stressful day in this world and go to sleep hoping for rest, but instead I get a long stressful day there, too. If it were more interesting I'd write books about it. But mostly I just want it to stop or become more useful (like communicating with others of you here as well).
